idiom_name: trait with default methods + composition for shared state
implementation_notes: Rust has no inheritance, so the layer's shared behavior is a trait with default methods: every member implements the trait - often with an empty impl block - and generic code or dyn LayerObject treats the layer uniformly, while blanket implementations add derived behavior for all members at once. Shared data cannot be inherited; it is composed as a struct field reached through a required accessor (or shared behind Arc), the explicit form of what a base class stores implicitly. When a design seems to demand a base class, split the two jobs inheritance bundled: reuse of state is composition, reuse of behavior is default trait methods.
pitfalls: A trait cannot store state: copying an id/version field into every implementor (or abusing Deref to fake inheritance) rebuilds a base class by hand and is usually better solved by composing a shared struct.
Default methods cannot be called from an overriding implementation, and generic bounds monomorphise, so stacking defaults on a hot trait grows code size.
dyn LayerObject requires object safety: generic methods or Self-returning signatures make the trait unusable behind a pointer unless the design accounts for it from the start.
